'''John Feather Wheater''' (born 1958, in [[London]]) is a British physicist. He is a professor at the [[University of Oxford]], specializing in [[particle physics]].<ref name="cv">{{cite web| url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2011-08-04/john_wheater_cv_2015_pdf_96715.pdf | title=Curriculum Vitae: John Feather WHEATER | publisher=[[Department of Physics, University of Oxford]] | first=John F. | last=Wheater | date=2015 | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/wheater | title=John Wheater | publisher=[[Department of Physics, University of Oxford]] | location=UK | access-date=20 April 2020 }}</ref><ref name="univ">{{cite web| url=https://www.univ.ox.ac.uk/academics/john-wheater/ | title=John Wheater | publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] | location=UK | access-date=20 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www-thphys.physics.ox.ac.uk/people/JohnWheater/ | title=John Wheater | publisher=Theoretical Physics, [[University of Oxford]] | location=UK | access-date=20 April 2020 }}</ref>

==Education==
Wheater was educated at [[St Paul's School, London]] and the [[University of Oxford]], where he read [[Physics]] at [[Christ Church, Oxford|Christ Church]] from 1976 to 1979, graduating with a first class degree and winning the Scott Prize for Physics.<ref name="cv" /> He undertook a [[DPhil]] degree on [[electroweak]] radiative corrections, supervised by [[Chris Llewellyn Smith]], from 1979 to 1981.<ref name="academictree">{{cite web| url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=453632 | title=John F. Wheater | work=Physics Tree | publisher=[[Academic Tree]] | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Wheater was a [[Junior Research Fellow]] in [[theoretical physics]] at Christ Church during 1981–84. In 1984–85, he was a lecturer in [[theoretical particle physics]] at [[Durham University]].

In 1985, Wheater joined the academic staff of the [[Department of Physics, University of Oxford|Department of Physics]] at Oxford University, initially as a lecturer. He was also a [[Fellow (college)|fellow]] of [[University College, Oxford]], from 1985 until 2015.<ref name="univ" /> During 1990 and later in 2003–4, he was on sabbatical leave spent at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] in [[Copenhagen]], Denmark. In 1993, he was awarded the [[Maxwell Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name="maxwell">{{cite web| url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/early-career/maxwell/medallists/page_38660.html | title=Maxwell medal recipients | publisher=[[Institute of Physics]] | access-date=11 April 2020 }}</ref> He was Head of the Physics Department between 2010 and 2018. In 2015, he was appointed as Professor of Physics. Wheater leads the Particle Theory Group.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/research/particle-theory | title=Particle Theory | publisher=[[Department of Physics, University of Oxford]] | location=UK | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref>

[[File:Beecroft Bldg Oxford.jpg|thumb|The [[Beecroft Building]], part of the Department of Physics, opened in 2018 under Wheater's leadership]]
During Wheater's term as Head of the Department of Physics, the new [[Beecroft Building]] in the department was initiated.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.planetpartitioning.co.uk/planet-partitioning-secure-contract-for-beecroft-building/ | title=Planet Partitioning secure contract for University of Oxford's the Beecroft building | publisher=Planet Partitioning | location=UK | date=14 March 2017 | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.hawkinsbrown.com/projects/the-beecroft-building | title=Beecroft Building, University of Oxford | publisher=[[Hawkins\Brown]] | date=2020 | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref> It was opened in 2018 by Sir [[Tim Berners-Lee]] (who formerly studied physics at Oxford),<ref name="dop">{{cite web| url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/the-beecroft-building | title=The Beecroft Building | publisher=[[Department of Physics, University of Oxford]] | location=UK | access-date=11 April 2020 }}</ref> in the presence of Wheater as Head of department, Professor [[Louise Richardson]] ([[Vice-Chancellor of Oxford]]), [[Chris Patten]] ([[Chancellor of Oxford]]), and [[Adrian Beecroft]] (part-funder of the building).<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OsuMz-Ep7gQ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/OsuMz-Ep7gQ |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live| title=The opening of Oxford's Beecroft Building | author=University of Oxford | author-link=University of Oxford | publisher=[[YouTube]] | date=27 September 2018 | access-date=11 April 2020 }}{{cbignore}}</ref>

In 2018–19, Wheater was invited to be a visiting professor at the QMATH-center in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at the [[University of Copenhagen]], Denmark.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.math.ku.dk/english/about/news/new-names/john-wheater-qmath/ | title=Professor John Wheater, guest at QMATH | publisher=Department of Mathematical Sciences, [[University of Copenhagen]] | location=Denmark | date=21 December 2018 | access-date=11 April 2020 }}</ref><ref name="orcid">{{cite web| url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1557-7091 | title=John Wheater | publisher=[[ORCID]] | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref>

Wheater's former doctoral students include [[Neil Ferguson (epidemiologist)|Neil Ferguson]],<ref name=ndphil/> who initially studied physics at Oxford University, but later became an epidemiologist and professor of [[mathematical biology]] at [[Imperial College London]] and was an influential scientist in the [[UK government]] strategy for the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.ft.com/content/7e56cf84-6a9e-11ea-a3c9-1fe6fedcca75 | title=Neil Ferguson, a virus modeller sounds the alarm | newspaper=[[Financial Times]] | first=Pilita | last=Clark | date=20 March 2020 | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref>

===Selected publications===
Wheater publications<ref name="cv" /><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/wheater/publications | title=John Wheater – publications | publisher=[[Department of Physics, University of Oxford]] | location=UK | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://arxiv.org/a/wheater_j_1.html | title=John F. Wheater's articles on arXiv | work=[[arXiv]] | publisher=[[Cornell University]] | location=USA | access-date=10 April 2020 }}</ref> include:

* Low-energy predictions from grand unified theories<ref>[[Christopher Llewellyn Smith|C.H.L. Smith]], [[Graham Ross (physicist)|G.G. Ross]], J.F. Wheater, Low-energy predictions from grand unified theories. ''[[Nuclear Physics B]]'', 1981. {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(81)90391-6}}</ref>
* C.H.L. Smith, J.F. Wheater, Electroweak radiative corrections and the value of sin2θW. ''[[Physics Letters B]]'', 1981.
* J.F. Wheater, C.H.L. Smith, Electroweak radiative corrections to neutrino and electron scattering and the value of sin2θW. ''Nuclear Physics B'', 1982.
* I.I. Kogan, N.E. Mavromatos, J.F. Wheater, D-brane recoil and logarithmic operators. ''Physics Letters B'', 1996.
* P. Austing, J.F. Wheater, Convergent Yang-Mills matrix theories. ''[[Journal of High Energy Physics]]'', 2001.

==Personal life==
Wheater is married with two daughters.<ref name="cv" />
